# Manifold reconciliation

This is the current interpretation of the existing findings after the owner's narrowed theoretical scope and authorized documentation reconciliation. The original reviews remain historical evidence. The shared [task ledger](../../source-locators.md#source-b7fdccb96a6dde23) owns current task status and each finding's recorded disposition; this page explains the reasons, repairs and limits.

The core questions already have written answers: what Manifold is for; the meanings of needs, requirements, systems, structure and process; their relationships; and scoped fulfillment. The [accepted notation](../standard/foundations/mathematical-notation.md), [adequacy rule](../standard/ontology/concepts/requirement.md#from-requirement-fulfillment-to-need-fulfillment) and [environment boundary](decisions/environment-specific-system-arrangements.md) are the baseline. Draft standing does not make a written answer absent, and reconciliation does not adopt the whole draft.

## Current scope and standing

The present deliverable defines Manifold and its theoretical representation. It does not complete the proposed S1/S2 application procedure, an intake/interview engine, storage and consumer contracts, a universal authority or state machine, or empirical interpreter studies. Particular owners, handlers, system combinations, criteria and operating conditions come from the environment.

The meaning of the dispositions below is local to this reconciliation:

- **Resolved:** the located inconsistency is repaired or an existing accepted rule supplies the answer, within the stated scope. A repaired candidate definition keeps its candidate standing.
- **Environment:** the specific selection belongs to the case under the accepted boundary; it is not a universal rule to invent here. Unstated case facts still limit conclusions.
- **Outside scope:** a broader proposal or study remains unfinished, but is not required to define the current core. This does not claim that its missing contract exists.
- **Remaining gap:** a consequential ambiguity still affects the current core. None remains from the findings reconciled below after the scoped wording repairs. This is a bounded conclusion, not proof that every future application is unambiguous.

## Concrete repairs and counterexamples

| Repair | Distinguishing example and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Classify the process, execution and description explicitly. | The weekly-review activity is a process; Monday's run is an execution; the page explaining it is a description. Document classification does not make the activity a document. |
| Separate structure from structural description. | The arrangement of components is structure; a diagram represents it. Changing the diagram does not establish a changed operating arrangement. |
| Separate a decision from its record. | A choice and the retained account of it are distinct. The record does not by itself prove the choosing act or its authority. |
| Describe authority without granting it by description. | Naming a role on a process page does not itself authorize its holder to approve an exception. The applicable authority basis remains a case fact. |
| Clarify requirement versus prediction. | A selected 250 ms limit is a criterion; predicting 250 ms performance does not by itself select that criterion or establish fulfillment. Proposed/adopted standing remains separate. |
| Make denominator relevance conditional. | A 250 ms scalar limit needs units; a success proportion also needs its denominator. No denominator is invented for the scalar limit. |
| Separate a changed view from changed obligations. | Drawing an external handoff outside a system boundary does not discharge an existing delivery requirement. An actual obligation change needs its own basis. |
| Clarify unexamined versus not assessed. | Reporting unknown because offline operation was unexamined is an assessment of an evidence gap. It is distinct from no assessment having occurred. No new fulfillment result is introduced. |

The repairs are in [classification](../standard/taxonomy/classification-rules.md), [modeling views](../standard/foundations/modeling-views.md), [structure](../standard/ontology/concepts/structure.md), [decisions](../standard/ontology/concepts/decisions-and-evidence.md), [process](../standard/ontology/concepts/process.md), [requirements](../standard/ontology/concepts/requirement.md), [composition](../standard/mereology/composition-and-boundaries.md) and [assessment](../standard/assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md). EOM-02's stale open label and the undecided-name claim are also corrected. The [rename decision](../../source-locators.md#source-d0ab2d989102d784) supplies current and historical location meanings.

## Prose and notation comparison

| Case | Agreement and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Successful report review | Integrity, timing and readability are met; stipulated actual review supports need fulfillment. Representation links alone do not prove it. |
| Unsuccessful report review | Specified integrity and timing are met, while incompatible format prevents review. Need is unmet; no omitted requirement is retroactively invented as failed. |
| Ambiguous report review | Integrity and timing are met; reading versus editing/recalculation is unclear. Dependent judgments stay unknown and ambiguity is raised without prescribing a handler. |
| Two of three sections readable | When all three are required and the third is known unreadable, the criterion is unmet and readable-section extent is partial. An unknown third section instead limits the extent conclusion. |
| Parts and process participation | A stated part relation concerns its case boundary; process participation does not infer parthood or ownership. Context changes are explicit. |

These are conceptual comparisons of the [accepted examples](../standard/foundations/mathematical-notation.md#6-worked-example), not observed operating performance, a reader-agreement study or a formal proof.

## Completion boundary

MT-03 and MT-04 concern the theoretical structural and process proposals now present, with choices and limits explicit. MT-06 concerns incorporation of these dispositions and the prose/notation comparison. Their completion does not release a normative standard or close all broader EOM tasks. The original broader completion criteria and scoped human-acceptance requirements are retained in the ledger.

After incorporation and verification, documentation reconciliation is complete and none of these known findings leaves an unidentified blocker to the agreed theoretical core. Broader ontology formalization, application procedures, representation contracts, normative adoption and empirical validation remain separate work. A new concrete counterexample can reopen the affected scoped question without erasing this history.
